title: Finite arrows and etale projections of a clopen restriction
statement:
Let $T,U,R,B$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $U\to T$, $R\to T$, $B\to T$, and etale $T$-morphisms $s,t:R\to U$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_TU$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Set $U_B=U\times_TB$, $R_B=R\times_TB$, and let $s_B,t_B:R_B\to U_B$ be the induced morphisms. Let $V\subseteq U_B$ be open and closed with its induced scheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion], and assume the structure morphism $V\to B$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Put
$$C=V\times_{U_B,s_B}R_B\times_{t_B,U_B}V,$$
with its canonical endpoint maps $s_C,t_C:C\to V$. Then the canonical map $C\to V\times_BV$ is a closed immersion and is finite. The scheme $V\times_BV$ is finite over $B$, and $C\to B$ is finite. The canonical map $C\to R_B$ is an open immersion with open and closed image $s_B^{-1}(V)\cap t_B^{-1}(V)$. Both endpoint maps $s_C,t_C$ are etale. These assertions require no equivalence-relation hypothesis on $(s,t)$.

source.place: Tag 03X5 (lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper), closed-immersion specialization of the restricted-relation argument and finiteness of the object square; etale projection permanence as in the preceding lemma-quasi-finite-over-base.

proof.text: Put $D=U_B\times_BU_B$ and $E=V\times_BV$. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $D$ with $(U\times_TU)\times_TB$ and identifies $R_B$ with $R\times_{U\times_TU}D$: maps into either object specify the same compatible maps into $R$, $U$, and $B$. Likewise $C\cong R_B\times_DE$: a map into either side specifies $r:H\to R_B$ and $v_1,v_2:H\to V$ with $s_Br=iv_1$ and $t_Br=iv_2$, where $i:V\hookrightarrow U_B$. These identifications respect both endpoint maps.

source.place: Tag 03X5, lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper, inverse image of the object square; explicit universal-property identifications

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] to $j:R\to U\times_TU$ along $D\to U\times_TU$, and then to $R_B\to D$ along $E\to D$. By step 1 the resulting closed immersion is exactly the canonical endpoint map $C\to E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] it is finite.

The projection $E=V\times_BV\to V$ is the base change of the given finite map $V\to B$, so it is finite by clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Compose it with $V\to B$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] to obtain finiteness of $E\to B$. Compose this map with the finite map $C\to E$ from step 2, using the same composition lemma, to obtain finiteness of $C\to B$.

Pull back $i:V\hookrightarrow U_B$ first along $s_B$, and then along $t_B$ on that pullback. Both projections are open immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. An open immersion identifies its source with the indicated open subscheme by [def-weil-open-immersion]; consequently these two pullbacks are the successive restrictions to $s_B^{-1}(V)$ and to $W=s_B^{-1}(V)\cap t_B^{-1}(V)$. Their structure sheaves are the corresponding restrictions of $\mathcal O_{R_B}$. Thus $C$ is precisely the open subscheme $W$ of $R_B$, with canonical map the inclusion. Since morphisms of schemes are continuous, the inverse images of the open and closed subset $V$ are open and closed; their intersection $W$ is open and closed as asserted.

source.place: Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion); open subscheme interpretation of the restricted relation

proof.text: The maps $s_B,t_B$ are base changes of $s,t$: for example $R_B\cong R\times_{U,s}U_B$ by the compatible-map description of [def-pc-fibre-product]. They are therefore etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Set $A_s=R_B\times_{U_B,s_B}V$. The map $A_s\to V$ is etale by the same lemma. The inclusion $C\to A_s$ is an open immersion by step 4, hence etale by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Clause (2) gives that its composite $s_C:C\to V$ is etale. Interchanging $s_B$ and $t_B$ gives the same factorization and proof for $t_C$. Every construction above uses only the two endpoint maps, not identity, inverse or composition operations of a relation.

lean.statement: theorem finite_clopen_relation_projection_properties (T U R B : Scheme.{u}) (fU : U ⟶ T) (fR : R ⟶ T) (fB : B ⟶ T) (s t : R ⟶ U) (hs : s ≫ fU = fR) (ht : t ≫ fU = fR) [Etale s] [Etale t] [IsClosedImmersion (pullback.lift s t (hs.trans ht.symm))] (V : (pullback fU fB).Opens) (_hV : IsClosed (V : Set (pullback fU fB : Scheme.{u}))) [IsFinite (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd fU fB)] : IsClosedImmersion (toSquare fU fR fB s t hs ht V) ∧ IsFinite (toSquare fU fR fB s t hs ht V) ∧ IsFinite (pullback.fst (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd fU fB) (V.ι ≫ pullback.snd fU fB) ≫ V.ι ≫ pullback.snd fU fB) ∧ IsFinite (toRelation fU fR fB s t hs ht V ≫ pullback.snd fR fB) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (toRelation fU fR fB s t hs ht V) ∧ Set.range (toRelation fU fR fB s t hs ht V) = (baseChangeEndpoint fU fR fB s hs) ⁻¹' (V : Set (pullback fU fB : Scheme.{u})) ∩ (baseChangeEndpoint fU fR fB t ht) ⁻¹' (V : Set (pullback fU fB : Scheme.{u})) ∧ IsClopen (Set.range (toRelation fU fR fB s t hs ht V)) ∧ Etale (source fU fR fB s t hs ht V) ∧ Etale (target fU fR fB s t hs ht V)
